Article.ArticleTitle: Overview on Anticancer Drug Design and Development.

Abstract.AbstractText: Many impediments of current anti-cancer therapies have urged scientists to discover new agents. As a result of growing spectrums of new targets and strategies and recent biological and biotechnological progresses, many anti-cancer agents such as monoclonal antibodies, small molecule tyrosine kinase inhibitors and epigenetic drugs have been reached to clinical trials. Addition to the traditional targets (mitosis, DNA synthesis, repairing systems, tumor growth, apoptosis, tumor vasculature and cell signaling mechanisms), other targets such as proteasome, heat shock proteins (HSPs), and epigenetics (HDACs, HATs, DNMT, PAD4, AID, and Tet1) are used to design new anti-cancer agents. In this review, recent approaches of the target-based anti-cancer drug developments have been highlighted to giving some examples from approved agents. Many factors, such as metabolic change, hypoxia, cancer precursors and cancer resistant cells, and their effect on drug resistance mechanisms have been discussed. Importance of progress in computational methodologies especially simulation of bio-molecular processes to develop new potent anti-cancer drugs has been emphasized. Contributions of recent techniques such as a network analysis of cancer specific metabolisms and the precise modes of action (MoA) that help to understand tumor complexity and mechanism actions of anti-cancer drugs have been explained. This review provides an overview of important targets and design strategies of anti-cancer drugs, advantages and disadvantages of these methods and evaluation of some currently used anticancer targets in clinical studies.
